idea.title: Have you eaten?
idea.summary: A stranger's first Hindi message is 'have you eaten?', a caring way to say hello; translate in chat and a call teach the reply.
hookOptions: A stranger's first Hindi message: aapne khana khaya?
In India, hello can be a question about dinner
She texted me in Hindi. I only knew namaste.
A stranger taught me one Hindi phrase

scenes.text: A stranger's first Hindi message: aapne khana khaya?
scenes.say: A stranger opened with 'have you eaten?' Not hello.

scenes.name: Sunny Kettle
scenes.say: One tap translated it. That's how she says she cares.

scenes.name: Sunny Kettle
scenes.label: She laughed for a minute
scenes.say: I said haan out loud and she laughed.

scenes.sub: Yes, I've eaten. Thanks for asking.
scenes.say: Haan means yes. Now I'm basically family.
Your next phrase is one call away.

post.caption: In a lot of Indian homes, 'have you eaten?' means 'I care about you'. A stranger can teach you that in one chat. What's a phrase you learned from someone new? Try it at randomtalker.com
